record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.context_brief: L1 bounded-below test on ell1 subspaces
record.original_question: Let T : L^1(0,1) -> L^1(0,1) be a bounded operator. Suppose that for every subspace M of L^1(0,1) that is isometric to ell^1(N), the restriction T|M is an isomorphism in the bounded-below sense. Must T itself be an isomorphism in that same bounded-below sense?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $T : L^1(0,1) \to L^1(0,1)$ be a bounded linear operator. Recall that a bounded linear operator $S : X \to Y$ between Banach spaces is said to be bounded below (an isomorphism onto its range) if there exists a constant $c > 0$ such that $\|Sx\| \ge c\|x\|$ for every $x \in X$. Suppose that for every closed linear subspace $M \subseteq L^1(0,1)$ that is isometrically isomorphic to $\ell^1(\mathbb{N})$, the restriction $T|_M : M \to L^1(0,1)$ is bounded below. Must $T$ itself be bounded below on $L^1(0,1)$?
